report.description: A structured report with a running header, page numbers and a table of contents.

files.content/01-report.md:
# Report Title

A short summary of the document goes here. Replace this paragraph with the
abstract or executive summary of your report.

## Overview

Write the body of the report under a heading. Headings build the outline in
the sidebar and the running header at the top of each page.

### A subsection

Subheadings work the same way.

## Findings

| Metric | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coverage | 94% | Measured across the reference suite |
| Errors | 0 | No mismatches in the last run |

Add a table like the one above to present data.

## Next steps

1. Replace this section with your own.
2. Export the document as a PDF when it is ready.

article.name: Article
article.description: A long-form article in a serif face with pull quotes.

files.content/01-article.md:
# The Title of the Article

A subtitle or standfirst that tells the reader what the piece is about.

## The first section

An article reads differently from a report. It sets the scene, then argues a
point. The bundled serif face is used for the body text, while headings use
the sans face so they stand out.

> A pull quote goes here. It is set in italics with a rule down its left edge.

## The second section

Keep paragraphs short. If a paragraph runs past four or five lines, it is
usually two paragraphs.

### A subsection

Subheadings break up long arguments.

## Closing

End with the point the article was making.
